Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Equinox pilot: inference fit, SDK changes, function-calls & next steps

Hi Lina / Devon —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side with the specific asks we agreed would determine pilot scope and success criteria. Please flag or correct anything I get wrong.

Summary of pain & goals
- Latency at 99th: < 200ms for single-turn summarize & rerank requests (90% of traffic).
- Cost sensitivity: current target is <= $0.002/token averaged across production mix.
- Feature needs: streaming partials for user-visible experiences, function-calling for structured policy extraction, embeddings for similarity search and reranking of candidate answers.

Technical notes / constraints you shared
- Primary model size preference: 7B-13B family (quantized); on-prem possibility later.
- Typical context window: 4k tokens with many short prefixes (chatty prompts), ~10% long documents hitting 2–3k.
- KV cache reuse expected in multi-turn; desire persistent session affinity for performance.

Pilot scope we proposed / agreed
- 6-week pilot: integration of Redwood SDK into a single Equinox product flow (customer support triage).
- Deliverables: streaming summarize endpoint + function-call extractors, embedding index + reranker sample, perf/latency baseline, cost model.
- Success criteria: 1) streaming UX working end-to-end; 2) structured extractor correctly maps to schema at >= 85% precision on a 200-case eval set; 3) embedding reranker improves NDCG>0.12 vs baseline.

Immediate engineering asks (owners)
- Equinox: share 3 representative prompts + 200 eval examples for the structured extractor (Lina) — due 2026-08-12.
- Redwood: prototype streaming + function-call sample in our SDK repo; provide a small patch that shows how to enable streaming partials + funcall mapping (Ben/Karthik) — initial diff by 2026-08-10.
- Both: agree on redaction/PII handling and opt-in telemetry scope (Procurement/Legal).

Procurement & timeline
- Lina mentioned a procurement window that could start as early as mid-September; procurement contact is included below. We'll surface standard SOC2 docs and a pilot SOW draft.

Attachments: I attached a short MVP spec and our pricing framing for the pilot.

Next calls
- Tech sync (Redwood eng + Equinox eng): Monday 2026-08-10 10:00 PT (Ben / Karthik / Lina / Devon)
- Procurement intro (optional): week of 2026-08-17

Thanks — excited to get this running.

—
Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Equinox pilot: inference fit, SDK changes, function-calls & next steps

Thanks Ben — this is great and captures the call well. A couple of clarifications from our side:

1) Latency: 200ms 99th is for the summarize user flow (single-turn). For the reranker step we can tolerate up to 400ms at 95th — the reranker runs server-side after candidate generation.
2) Data: we'll provide the 200 eval cases but need guidance on how to sanitize customer PII. Do you have a recommended redaction script?
3) Function calling: our extractor schema has nested fields (customer.contact.phone). Can your function-call support nested/typed fields or do we need to flatten?

Action items from Equinox
- I'll send sanitized eval examples by 2026-08-12 (Lina).
- I'll confirm procurement window and introduce procurement@equinox.ai into the thread if the timeline holds (Devon).

Thanks — excited to see the SDK sample.

Best,
Lina Torres
VP Product, Equinox.ai
lina@equinox.ai

Lina — thanks for the clarifications, and good call on the nested schema. Short answers below and a plan: 

- Latency: noted (200ms/99th for summarize; 400ms/95th for rerank). We'll include both targets in the SLOs for the pilot.
- PII redaction: attaching a small Python redaction snippet we typically use; it removes emails/phones/SSN-like patterns and hashes IDs. We'll include it in the Drive folder too.
- Function-calls + nested fields: Redwood's current funcall mapping supports typed nested objects (we map to JSON Schema). For the pilot we'll provide an example mapping and run an integration test against your 200-case set. Karthik will own the mapping example.

Karthik — copying you to confirm you can produce the SDK sample and that the streaming + funcall example will be in the repo (branch: eqx/pilot-demo) by COB 2026-08-10.

Next steps (quick timeline)
- 2026-08-10: Redwood SDK sample (streaming + funcall) + redaction snippet (Ben/Karthik).
- 2026-08-12: Equinox uploads sanitized 200-case evaluation set + prompts (Lina).
- 2026-08-17: Tech sync with procurement (tentative) and pilot SOW draft.

Thanks — I'll push the branch and link the Drive resources ASAP.

—
Ben

Hi Ben / Marissa —

We reviewed the high-level pilot outline. A few procurement items to confirm before we proceed: 

1) Pilot SOW: needs a 6-week timeline, acceptance criteria, and a clause for data handling (we require logs to be turned off by default and explicit opt-in for telemetry).
2) Liability: Equinox requires a standard mutual indemnity paragraph; can you share your SSO and SOC2 report?
3) Pricing: can Redwood provide a capped pilot spend (we prefer a not-to-exceed PO)? The pricing spreadsheet was helpful but please confirm a hard cap.

Marissa — can you own the SOW draft and share a clean version to procurement by EOD Wed 2026-08-12? Ben / Karthik — please provide SOC2 pointer & the capped-cost figure for the pilot.
